training_history.opening: Mr. Kumar today. Fifty-two, stomach pain, and a terrible patient. Go on. Ask.

questions.ask: When did the pain start, and has it moved?
questions.answer: Last night, around my belly button. This morning it moved down here, low on the right.
questions.fact: Pain moved from belly button to low right
questions.why: Pain that starts at the belly button and moves low on the right is the classic story of appendicitis.

questions.answer: Penicillin. I came up in a rash once. Big one.
questions.why: He's allergic to penicillin. The usual antibiotic before surgery would have given him a reaction on the table.

questions.answer: A blood thinner. For my heart. And something for acidity, when I remember.
questions.why: He takes a blood thinner. Operate without knowing and he bleeds, a lot.

questions.ask: When did you last eat or drink?
questions.answer: Breakfast at eight. Two idlis and tea. Is that bad?
questions.why: He ate at eight. A full stomach under anaesthetic can come back up into the lungs, so surgery has to wait.

questions.ask: Show me exactly where it hurts.
questions.answer: Here. Sharp when I walk, worse when I cough. Don't press it. Don't.
questions.fact: Sharp low right, worse on coughing

questions.ask: Have you had any operations before?
questions.answer: My tonsils. I was eight. I still remember the ice cream.
I gave up smoking. Mostly. Weekends don't count.
Who doesn't? That's one question gone, Doctor. Patients get tired. So do I.
I'm a bank manager. Everything is stressful. It's not why my belly hurts.
